title: Eleven public ESPRESSO rows cannot separate two GJ 887 short-period models when four planet waves are free
abstract: We test the information in 11 public ESPRESSO velocities for the reported 2.21661-day GJ 887 candidate. With free sine and cosine coefficients for four known planet periods and one instrument constant, both the candidate model and a 2.21245-day harmonic model have rank 11 and fit all rows exactly. Residual fit cannot separate these unrestricted linear models. At the reported 0.37 m/s amplitude, assumed extra independent Gaussian noise of 1.6 m/s gives 1.23 percent mean power for a fixed-period test with 1 percent false-alarm size. Power ranges from 1.005 to 1.464 percent over phase. Even with the other waves known exactly, mean power is 1.73 percent. A 50000-trial simulation checks the calculation. These results do not confirm or exclude a planet. Exact eccentric orbits, informative priors and correlated stellar noise are outside the test. We provide original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and external retrieval steps. No source rows are bundled.

display.caption: Known-noise power at a fixed candidate period and principal coefficient errors. Lines on the left show uniform-phase mean power; shading shows the phase range. Four freely fitted planet waves give weak and strongly phase-dependent sensitivity. The 1.6 m/s extra noise is assumed, not measured here.
